evidence_for_holdout: zeroshot/generalization.toml in the model repo lists C32, HOP62, HepG2/C3A, Hs 766T and PANC-1 as zero-shot test cell types (sources/ST-HVG-Tahoe_zeroshot_generalization.toml).
The official run evaluated exactly these five lines as test (eval_best.ckpt/<line>_agg_results.csv; copies in sources/st_hvg_tahoe_zeroshot/).

cell-load@9ba45e5 PerturbationDataModule: zero-shot cell types are routed to the test split; val_dataloader() falls back to the test datasets when no validation split exists, so the held-out lines produced val_loss but no gradients.

version_0/metrics.csv: val_loss on the held-out lines was lowest at step 7,999 (0.1685) and rose to 0.64-0.84 by steps 148k-156k while train_loss fell to ~0.08; training on these lines would not produce a four-fold rise in their loss.
Training ended at step 157,749 (max_steps 200,000); final.ckpt is the end-of-training checkpoint and is not selected on validation.
residual_caveats: data_module.torch and config.yaml name /data/tahoe_se/generalization_zeroshot.toml, not the repo file name generalization.toml; the content match is inferred, not proven by a hash.
best.ckpt was selected on the held-out lines' val_loss and must not be used for held-out claims; this study uses final.ckpt only.
cell_type_onehot_map.pkl lists all 50 cell types; it is a global encoding map, not evidence of training use.
The pooled multiplexed design means the held-out lines' treated cells shared wells with training lines; STATE saw those wells' other lines.
development_diagnostic: STATE's leave-one-out deviation gain on training contexts (in-sample, median -37%) is similar to its gain on the held-out development lines (-42%, -35%); with the val_loss history this indicates little per-line overfitting of the mean deviation rather than leakage.
